title: Senior Frontend: scaling the frontend
blurb: For engineers going from mid to senior or staff: rendering and state architecture at scale, design systems, monorepos, micro-frontends, performance, testing strategy, frontend infrastructure, safe releases, security, i18n and leading frontend architecture.
audience: Mid-level frontend engineers aiming for senior or staff roles

nodes.title: Choosing rendering per route
nodes.summary: SSR, SSG, ISR, CSR and streaming chosen per route by freshness, personalisation and cost. Seniors are expected to justify the choice with numbers.
checklist: Compare CSR, SSR, SSG and ISR on TTFB, LCP, server cost and data freshness
Pick a rendering mode for a marketing page, a product page, a dashboard and a checkout and defend each
Explain how personalisation and auth cookies break static caching and how to work around it
Describe ISR revalidation by time and on demand (by path or tag) and what users see during regeneration
Estimate origin load for SSR vs SSG at a given request rate and cache-hit ratio
Explain why one app usually mixes several rendering modes route by route

nodes.title: Hydration, islands and resumability
nodes.summary: Hydration cost, partial and progressive hydration, islands and resumability, and how each shifts work between server and client. This is where most SSR performance is won or lost.
checklist: Explain what hydration does and why a server-rendered page can look ready but not respond to input
Measure hydration cost in a performance trace and relate it to TBT and INP
Contrast progressive hydration, selective hydration and islands
Explain resumability (Qwik) and how it avoids replaying component code on load
Diagnose and fix a hydration mismatch caused by dates, randomness or browser-only APIs
Decide when an islands framework like Astro beats a full React app

links.title: Next.js docs: Server and Client Components

nodes.title: React Server Components architecture
nodes.summary: Server Components run only on the server and ship no JavaScript, while Client Components hydrate. Knowing where to draw the boundary is now a core senior React skill.
checklist: Explain what the RSC payload is and how it differs from HTML
Place the 'use client' boundary as low as possible and explain why props crossing it must be serialisable
Pass Server Components as children into Client Components to avoid client-izing a subtree
Fetch data in Server Components without request waterfalls (parallel fetches, preloading)
Explain how Server Functions ('use server') are invoked and why they need auth checks like any endpoint
List what cannot run in a Server Component (state, effects, browser APIs) and why

links.title: Josh Comeau: making sense of React Server Components
Next.js docs: Server and Client Components

nodes.title: Streaming SSR and Suspense
nodes.summary: Streaming sends the shell first and fills slow parts as their data arrives, using Suspense boundaries. It turns one slow query from a blank page into a skeleton.
checklist: Explain how chunked HTML streaming works and why TTFB improves
Choose Suspense boundary placement so the shell is useful and layout does not shift
Use loading.tsx and nested Suspense in the Next.js App Router
Explain selective hydration: how React prioritises the boundary the user interacts with
Use transitions (useTransition) to keep old UI visible instead of flashing fallbacks
Know what breaks streaming: buffering proxies, response compression settings and late headers

links.title: React 18 working group: new Suspense SSR architecture

nodes.title: Partial prerendering and cache components
nodes.summary: Static shells with streamed dynamic holes in Next.js, configured through cache components and 'use cache'. Worth knowing; framework-specific and still evolving.
checklist: Explain the static shell plus dynamic holes model and what it does to TTFB and LCP
Enable cache components and mark cached work with 'use cache' and cache lifetimes
Explain which APIs (cookies, headers, searchParams) make a component dynamic
Invalidate cached data by tag after a mutation
Compare PPR with classic ISR plus client-side fetching for personalised pages

nodes.title: Edge rendering and CDN caching
nodes.summary: Cache keys, stale-while-revalidate at the CDN, edge vs regional compute and what not to run at the edge. The cheapest request is the one the origin never sees.
checklist: Write Cache-Control for hashed assets, HTML and API responses and explain each directive
Explain s-maxage, stale-while-revalidate and stale-if-error at a CDN
Design cache keys that vary on the right things (locale, device class) without fragmenting the cache
Purge by URL vs by surrogate key or tag and know the trade-offs
Explain why per-user HTML should not be cached at a shared CDN and how cookies affect this
Measure cache-hit ratio and origin offload and set a target

links.title: web.dev: keeping things fresh with stale-while-revalidate
RFC 5861: HTTP Cache-Control extensions for stale content

nodes.title: Edge functions and their limits
nodes.summary: Edge runtimes run code in V8 isolates close to users, but with limited APIs and far from your database. Seniors know which work belongs at the edge and which does not.
checklist: Explain the isolate model and why edge cold starts are smaller than container cold starts
List edge runtime limits: no full Node APIs, CPU time caps, bundle size limits
Explain why SSR at the edge can be slower when the database is in one region
Pick good edge jobs: redirects, auth gating, geolocation, A/B bucketing, header rewrites
Use Next.js proxy.ts for optimistic redirects while keeping real auth checks next to data

nodes.title: A state taxonomy
nodes.summary: Server cache, URL, form, local UI and global client state each get a different tool. Most scaling pain is server state stored in a global store.
checklist: Classify a given piece of state as server, URL, form, local UI or global client state
Explain why server state needs caching, deduping and invalidation rather than a reducer
Move filters, tabs and pagination into the URL so views are shareable and survive refresh
Keep form state local to the form and validate with a schema
Argue when a global client store is still justified (auth session, theme, cross-route drafts)

links.title: Kent C. Dodds: application state management with React

nodes.title: Server-state caching
nodes.summary: Libraries like TanStack Query and SWR treat fetched data as a cache with keys, staleness and invalidation. Getting the keys and invalidation right removes most data bugs.
checklist: Design hierarchical query keys and invalidate by prefix after a mutation
Explain staleTime vs gcTime and choose values per data type
Deduplicate concurrent requests and explain request waterfalls vs parallel queries
Prefetch on hover or on the server and hydrate the client cache
Handle pagination and infinite queries without refetching every page
Explain how server-state caching interacts with RSC and framework caches

links.title: TkDodo: React Query as a state manager

nodes.title: State architecture for large apps
nodes.summary: Normalisation, selectors, colocating state, cross-team state contracts and avoiding re-render storms. This is what keeps a 200-screen app maintainable.
checklist: Normalise nested entities by id and explain what bugs this prevents
Write memoised selectors and explain how they avoid needless re-renders
Colocate state at the lowest common owner and lift it only when needed
Explain why a single large React context re-renders every consumer and how to split it
Compare Redux Toolkit, Zustand and Jotai on boundaries, devtools and subscription granularity
Define state ownership contracts between teams so one team cannot mutate another's slice

links.title: react.dev: scaling up with reducer and context

nodes.title: Optimistic updates and realtime data
nodes.summary: Optimistic UI shows the result before the server confirms, and realtime channels push changes from others. Together they decide whether an app feels instant and stays consistent.
checklist: Implement an optimistic update with rollback on error
Use useOptimistic with a Server Function or form action
Choose between polling, SSE and WebSockets for a given update rate and direction
Merge pushed events into a client cache without duplicates or out-of-order overwrites
Handle reconnects: resume from a cursor and refetch what was missed

nodes.title: State machines for complex flows
nodes.summary: Modelling checkout, uploads and wizards as explicit states and transitions so impossible states cannot happen.
checklist: Replace a set of isLoading/isError booleans with a discriminated union of states
Draw a statechart for a checkout or file upload flow, including cancel and retry
Explain guards, actions and parallel states
Decide when a reducer with a union type is enough and when XState earns its weight

links.title: Kent C. Dodds: stop using isLoading booleans

nodes.title: Offline and sync
nodes.summary: Optimistic updates, retry queues, conflict resolution and local-first data. Needed for field, chat and editor products.
checklist: Store data locally in IndexedDB and explain its limits and eviction
Queue writes while offline and replay them idempotently on reconnect
Compare last-write-wins, field-level merge and CRDTs for conflicts
Cache the app shell with a service worker and choose a caching strategy per request type
Explain the local-first ideals and where they are hard in practice

nodes.title: Design system foundations
nodes.summary: Tokens, primitives, theming, component API design and versioning. The highest-leverage frontend platform investment.
checklist: Explain the layers: tokens, primitives, components, patterns and templates
Design a component API with composition (slots, compound components) instead of a prop explosion
Decide what belongs in the system vs in a product team's code
Support controlled and uncontrolled usage and forward refs and native props
Document components with usage guidance, do and don't examples and accessibility notes

nodes.title: Design tokens and theming
nodes.summary: Tokens turn colour, spacing and type decisions into data that compiles to CSS variables, iOS and Android. Theming and dark mode become a token swap instead of a rewrite.
checklist: Separate primitive tokens (blue-500) from semantic tokens (color-bg-danger)
Build tokens to CSS custom properties with Style Dictionary or a similar tool
Implement light, dark and high-contrast themes without a flash of the wrong theme
Respect prefers-color-scheme and prefers-reduced-motion
Support multi-brand theming from one component library
Check token colour pairs against WCAG contrast ratios automatically

links.title: Josh Comeau: the quest for the perfect dark mode

nodes.title: Headless and accessible primitives
nodes.summary: Separating behaviour from styling (Radix, React Aria) so accessibility is solved once.
checklist: Explain what a headless component provides (state, keyboard, ARIA) and what it leaves to you
Implement a dialog with focus trap, focus return and Escape to close
Follow the ARIA Authoring Practices pattern for a combobox, menu or tabs
Compare Radix, React Aria and Base UI on API style and coverage
Explain why rebuilding a select or combobox from scratch is risky

nodes.title: Accessibility at scale
nodes.summary: Accessibility across dozens of teams needs automated checks, manual audits and ownership. Automated tools catch only part of WCAG failures, so process matters as much as tooling.
checklist: Run axe checks in component tests, Storybook and Playwright in CI
Explain which WCAG failures automation cannot catch and how manual testing covers them
Test key flows with a screen reader (VoiceOver or NVDA) and keyboard only
Set WCAG 2.2 AA as the bar and track violations as bugs with owners
Explain legal drivers (ADA, European Accessibility Act) at a high level

nodes.title: Running a design system at scale
nodes.summary: Governance, contribution models, adoption metrics, deprecations and codemods across many teams.
checklist: Compare centralised, federated and hybrid contribution models
Measure adoption (component usage scans, detached overrides) and act on it
Run a deprecation: warn, provide a codemod, set a removal date
Keep design files and code in sync and define who owns the source of truth
Write an RFC process for new components

links.title: Brad Frost: the design system ecosystem

nodes.title: Versioning and releasing shared packages
nodes.summary: Semantic versioning, changelogs and release automation decide whether teams can upgrade a shared library safely. Breaking changes need a migration path, not just a major bump.
checklist: Apply semver to a component library and classify changes as patch, minor or major
Automate changelogs and releases with Changesets
Explain the trade-off between independent and fixed versioning in a monorepo
Avoid duplicate React or design-system copies with peer dependencies
Ship breaking changes behind codemods and deprecation warnings

nodes.title: Visual regression testing
nodes.summary: Screenshot diffs on every component change to catch unintended UI breakage.
checklist: Set up screenshot tests for components and key pages
Make screenshots deterministic: fonts, animations, dates and dynamic data
Pick a diff threshold and review workflow so diffs are approved, not ignored
Compare self-hosted Playwright snapshots with a hosted service like Chromatic

nodes.title: Monorepos and task runners
nodes.summary: Workspaces, task graphs, remote caching, affected-only CI and package boundaries. The difference between a 4-minute and a 40-minute CI.
checklist: Set up pnpm workspaces with internal packages and explain workspace protocol versions
Define a task graph (build depends on ^build) in Turborepo or Nx
Explain content-hash task caching and turn on remote caching in CI
Run only affected packages on a pull request
Enforce package boundaries so apps cannot import each other's internals
Compare Turborepo and Nx on scope, plugins and generators

nodes.title: TypeScript at scale
nodes.summary: Large codebases need project references, strict settings and fast type checks. Type-check time is a real CI and editor cost at scale.
checklist: Split a codebase with project references and composite builds
Diagnose slow type checks with --extendedDiagnostics and --generateTrace
Choose shared tsconfig bases for apps, libraries and tests
Enforce module boundaries with lint rules
Roll out stricter compiler flags incrementally

nodes.title: Bundlers and the build pipeline
nodes.summary: How Vite, webpack, Rspack and Turbopack differ: dev server model, HMR, chunking and build caching.
checklist: Explain unbundled ESM dev servers vs bundled dev servers
Explain how HMR keeps state and when it falls back to a full reload
Configure code splitting and explain how chunk hashing enables long-term caching
Explain why Rust- and Go-based tools (Rspack, Turbopack, esbuild) are faster
Plan a webpack to Vite or Rspack migration and list what usually breaks

nodes.title: Codemods and large refactors
nodes.summary: AST-based migrations with jscodeshift or ts-morph to change thousands of files safely.
checklist: Explore code as an AST in AST Explorer
Write a jscodeshift transform that renames an import and its usages
Use ts-morph when the change needs type information
Test a codemod with input and output fixtures and run it in batches

nodes.title: Monorepos vs micro-frontends
nodes.summary: When one repo with shared packages beats independently deployed apps, and the costs of each.
checklist: Separate the code-sharing problem (monorepo) from the independent-deploy problem (micro-frontends)
List the organisational signals that justify independent deploys
Compare a modular monolith frontend with route-level micro-frontends on cost and speed
Explain how both approaches handle a shared design system

nodes.title: Micro-frontend patterns
nodes.summary: Build-time vs run-time composition, Module Federation, route-level splits and shared dependencies.
checklist: Compare build-time packages, run-time composition, iframes and server-side composition
Split by route or business domain rather than by UI widget
Design communication between micro-frontends (URL, custom events, a thin shared contract)
Keep routing owned by a shell and let each app own its sub-routes
Explain how styles are isolated to avoid CSS collisions

nodes.title: Module Federation in practice
nodes.summary: Module Federation loads code from separately deployed builds at runtime and shares dependencies like React between them. Powerful, but version drift and runtime failures are the price.
checklist: Configure a host and a remote and explain the remote entry file
Share singletons like React with version ranges and explain what happens on mismatch
Handle a remote that fails to load with an error boundary and fallback
Type remote modules and keep contracts in sync
Explain Next.js multi-zones as a simpler route-level alternative

nodes.title: When not to use micro-frontends
nodes.summary: Duplicate runtimes, inconsistent UX and harder debugging. Interviewers want to hear you push back when team size does not justify it.
checklist: List the costs: bundle duplication, inconsistent UX, cross-app debugging, integration testing
Explain why a small team rarely benefits from independent deploys
Propose cheaper alternatives: modular monolith, ownership rules, CODEOWNERS
Describe how to merge micro-frontends back when they no longer pay off

nodes.title: Core Web Vitals in the field
nodes.summary: LCP, INP and CLS measured on real users at the 75th percentile decide search ranking and user experience. Seniors must know the thresholds and the causes of each.
checklist: State the good thresholds: LCP 2.5 s, INP 200 ms, CLS 0.1, at p75
Break LCP into TTFB, resource load delay, load time and render delay
Break INP into input delay, processing time and presentation delay
List common CLS causes: images without dimensions, late ads, web fonts, injected banners
Read CrUX data for an origin and explain why it differs from Lighthouse

nodes.title: Bundle performance and budgets
nodes.summary: Budgets in CI, bundle analysis, splitting, tree-shaking, third-party governance and modern-only builds.
checklist: Set a JavaScript budget per route and fail CI when it is exceeded
Read a bundle analyser report and find the three biggest wins
Split by route and lazy-load below-the-fold or interaction-only code
Explain what breaks tree-shaking (side effects, CommonJS) and how to fix it
Govern third-party scripts: owners, budgets, loading strategy and removal
Drop legacy polyfills with a modern browserslist target

links.title: web.dev: reduce JavaScript payloads with code splitting

nodes.title: Images, fonts and CDN strategy
nodes.summary: Images are usually the LCP element and the largest bytes on the page. Responsive images, modern formats, priority hints and an image CDN fix most loading problems.
checklist: Serve responsive images with srcset and sizes and explain how the browser picks one
Choose AVIF or WebP with fallbacks and set quality per use case
Prioritise the LCP image with fetchpriority and avoid lazy-loading it
Use an image CDN for on-the-fly resizing and format negotiation
Load web fonts without layout shift (font-display, preload, size-adjust)

nodes.title: Real-user monitoring pipeline
nodes.summary: RUM collects vitals and errors from real sessions, tagged with route, device and release, so you can see regressions labs miss. It is how you prove a fix worked.
checklist: Collect LCP, INP and CLS with the web-vitals library and attribution builds
Send beacons reliably on page hide with sendBeacon or fetch keepalive
Tag events with route, release, device class and connection type
Report p75 and p95 per route and segment, not a single global average
Set alerts on vitals regressions after a deploy
Sample to control cost without losing small segments

links.title: web.dev: debug performance in the field

nodes.title: Performance engineering
nodes.summary: RUM vs lab, Core Web Vitals in the field, profiling long tasks and proving a fix with before/after data.
checklist: Explain why lab and field numbers differ and when to trust each
Record and read a DevTools performance trace: main thread, network, frames
Find the slow interaction behind a poor INP and fix it
Run a performance investigation as hypothesis, change and before/after measurement
Present a performance win in business terms (conversion, bounce, revenue)

links.title: web.dev: why lab and field data can be different

nodes.title: Keeping the main thread free
nodes.summary: Yielding, scheduling, Web Workers and virtualisation for heavy UIs like grids and editors.
checklist: Explain the 50 ms long-task threshold and why it matters for input
Break up long tasks with scheduler.yield or setTimeout and keep work ordered
Move parsing or computation to a Web Worker and pass data efficiently
Virtualise a list of 10,000 rows
Use React transitions and deferred values to keep typing responsive

nodes.title: Memory leaks in long-lived SPAs
nodes.summary: Detached DOM, lingering listeners and closures; using heap snapshots to find them.
checklist: List common leak sources: listeners, timers, detached DOM, caches without limits
Take and compare heap snapshots to find retained objects
Use the allocation timeline to find what keeps growing
Clean up subscriptions in effects and verify with a repeat-the-action test

links.title: Nolan Lawson: fixing memory leaks in web applications

nodes.title: A testing strategy for many teams
nodes.summary: What each layer catches, the testing trophy, flake budgets and keeping CI under ten minutes.
checklist: Explain what static, unit, integration and end-to-end tests each catch
Argue for integration-heavy component tests using Testing Library principles
Set ownership: who writes and maintains which test layer
Keep CI fast with sharding, caching and affected-only test runs
Track test health metrics: duration, flake rate, escaped bugs

links.title: Kent C. Dodds: the testing trophy
Martin Fowler: the practical test pyramid

nodes.title: API mocking and contract tests
nodes.summary: MSW for realistic network mocks and typed contracts so frontend and backend do not drift.
checklist: Mock the network at the request level with MSW in tests and local dev
Generate types and mocks from an OpenAPI schema
Explain consumer-driven contract testing with Pact
Catch breaking API changes in CI before they reach production

nodes.title: End-to-end tests at scale
nodes.summary: A few hundred reliable end-to-end tests protect critical journeys; a few thousand flaky ones slow everyone down. Scale needs isolation, parallelism and good selectors.
checklist: Choose which journeys deserve end-to-end coverage
Use role-based locators and web-first assertions instead of sleeps
Isolate test data per worker and reuse authenticated state
Shard tests across CI machines and merge reports
Run smoke tests against preview deployments and production

nodes.title: Managing flaky tests
nodes.summary: A flaky test fails sometimes without a code change, and at scale flakes erode trust in CI. Detect, quarantine and fix them with a clear owner and budget.
checklist: List root causes: timing, shared state, test order, network and animation
Detect flakes by re-running failures and tracking per-test failure rates
Quarantine flaky tests with an owner and a deadline instead of silently retrying
Debug a flake with traces, videos and repeat-each runs
Set and enforce a flake budget for the suite

links.title: Google Testing Blog: flaky tests at Google
Martin Fowler: eradicating non-determinism in tests

nodes.title: CI/CD for frontend
nodes.summary: A frontend pipeline lints, type-checks, tests, builds and deploys every change, with caching so it stays fast. Seniors own the pipeline's speed and reliability.
checklist: Lay out pipeline stages: install, lint, typecheck, test, build, deploy
Cache dependencies and build outputs between runs
Run Lighthouse CI or bundle-size checks on pull requests
Gate merges on required checks and keep main always deployable
Upload source maps and tag releases as part of the deploy

nodes.title: Preview environments
nodes.summary: Every pull request gets its own deployed URL for review, QA and automated tests. They shorten feedback loops but need safe data and secrets.
checklist: Explain how per-branch preview deployments are created and torn down
Point previews at safe backends or seeded data, never production writes
Protect previews from public access and search indexing
Run end-to-end and visual tests against the preview URL

nodes.title: Edge config and runtime configuration
nodes.summary: Some settings (flags, redirects, kill switches) must change without a deploy and be read in milliseconds at the edge. Edge key-value stores serve that need.
checklist: Separate build-time config from runtime config and secrets
Read low-latency config at the edge for redirects, flags or maintenance mode
Explain the consistency model of edge key-value stores and propagation delay
Design a safe default when config cannot be read

nodes.title: Frontend observability
nodes.summary: Error tracking, RUM, source maps, session context and alerting on user-facing metrics, not just server health.
checklist: Explain what errors, vitals, traces and session context each tell you
Propagate trace context from browser to backend to follow one request
Alert on user-facing symptoms (error rate, failed checkout) rather than causes
Build a release health view: crash-free sessions and errors by version
Keep personal data out of logs, replays and events

nodes.title: Error tracking and source maps
nodes.summary: Capture uncaught errors and rejections, group them, and map minified stack traces back to source. Without this, production bugs are guesswork.
checklist: Capture window error and unhandledrejection events plus React error boundaries
Upload source maps privately and tie them to a release id
Group and deduplicate errors and filter browser-extension noise
Attach breadcrumbs and context without leaking personal data
Triage errors by user impact, not raw count

nodes.title: Feature flags
nodes.summary: Release vs experiment flags, kill switches, flag debt and evaluating flags without layout shift.
checklist: Distinguish release, experiment, ops (kill switch) and permission flags
Evaluate flags on the server or at the edge to avoid flicker and layout shift
Keep flag evaluation consistent for a user across sessions and devices
Clean up flags with owners and expiry dates to control flag debt
Use OpenFeature to avoid vendor lock-in

nodes.title: Canaries and progressive rollouts
nodes.summary: Percent rollouts, automatic rollback on error-rate regressions and versioned assets so old tabs keep working.
checklist: Roll out by percentage, region or cohort and define promotion criteria
Compare canary error rates and vitals against the baseline
Roll back automatically when a metric crosses a threshold
Compare canary, blue-green and flag-based releases

nodes.title: Version skew and long-lived tabs
nodes.summary: After a deploy, open tabs still run old code that requests new or deleted assets and APIs. Handling skew prevents chunk-load errors and broken Server Actions.
checklist: Explain why old chunks 404 after a deploy and how to keep previous assets available
Recover from ChunkLoadError with a reload prompt or automatic retry
Keep APIs backward compatible for at least one release
Use skew protection or deployment ids to pin a session to one version
Update service workers safely without stranding users on old code

nodes.title: A/B testing
nodes.summary: Assignment, sample size and why peeking at results lies. Needed on growth teams.
checklist: Assign users to variants deterministically and avoid flicker
Estimate sample size from baseline rate and minimum detectable effect
Explain why peeking and stopping early inflates false positives
Choose guardrail metrics like errors and vitals alongside the goal metric

links.title: Evan Miller: how not to run an A/B test

nodes.title: Frontend security at scale
nodes.summary: XSS, strict CSP with nonces, Trusted Types, clickjacking and safe auth token handling.
checklist: Explain stored, reflected and DOM XSS and how frameworks escape output
Deploy a strict nonce-based CSP, starting in report-only mode
Enforce Trusted Types to lock down DOM sinks like innerHTML
Prevent clickjacking with frame-ancestors
Sanitise user HTML (DOMPurify) when it must be rendered

links.title: web.dev: mitigate XSS with a strict CSP

nodes.title: Auth patterns for web apps
nodes.summary: Where tokens live decides your exposure to XSS and CSRF. Seniors should defend HttpOnly cookie sessions or a backend-for-frontend over tokens in localStorage.
checklist: Compare HttpOnly cookies with tokens in localStorage under XSS
Set Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite attributes and explain each
Defend against CSRF with SameSite, tokens and origin checks
Explain the backend-for-frontend pattern for OAuth in browser apps
Handle session expiry and silent refresh without leaking tokens
Check authorization on the server for every action, not just in the UI

nodes.title: Supply-chain security
nodes.summary: Lockfiles, dependency review, Subresource Integrity and limiting third-party scripts.
checklist: Commit lockfiles and install with frozen lockfiles in CI
Review new dependencies for maintenance, size and install scripts
Automate updates and vulnerability alerts (Dependabot or Renovate)
Use Subresource Integrity for scripts loaded from CDNs
Explain npm provenance and why it helps verify packages

nodes.title: Internationalisation and localisation
nodes.summary: Message catalogues, ICU plurals, Intl formatting, locale routing and translation workflows.
checklist: Format dates, numbers, currencies and relative times with Intl
Write ICU messages with plurals and select instead of string concatenation
Route by locale and negotiate it from URL, cookie and Accept-Language
Load only the active locale's messages to keep bundles small
Run a translation workflow: extraction, translation service, pseudo-localisation

nodes.title: Right-to-left and logical properties
nodes.summary: CSS logical properties and bidi text so layouts flip correctly for Arabic and Hebrew.
checklist: Set dir and lang on the document and on mixed-direction content
Replace left and right with logical properties like margin-inline-start
Decide which icons should mirror in RTL and which should not
Handle bidi text in user content with dir=auto and bdi

links.title: W3C: structural markup and right-to-left text

nodes.title: RFCs and ADRs
nodes.summary: Writing design docs that get decisions made and recording them so the next team knows why.
checklist: Write an RFC with context, goals, non-goals, options and a recommendation
Record a decision as an ADR with status, context and consequences
Run a review that ends in a decision instead of endless comments
Keep decision records discoverable next to the code

links.title: The Pragmatic Engineer: RFCs and design docs

nodes.title: Running large migrations
nodes.summary: Strangler-fig migrations, incremental adoption, codemods and measuring progress to done.
checklist: Plan a strangler-fig migration route by route or component by component
Automate the bulk of the change with codemods and leave the hard tail to owners
Track progress with a metric and a burn-down visible to all teams
Stop new usage of the old way with lint rules
Explain why migrations stall at 80% and how to finish them

nodes.title: Technical strategy and influence
nodes.summary: Senior and staff engineers set direction across teams without authority, through written strategy, quality programmes and alignment. This is what the promotion committee looks for.
checklist: Write a short technical strategy: diagnosis, guiding policy, actions
Build alignment with stakeholders before a proposal is reviewed
Run a technical-quality programme with metrics and owners
Say no to good ideas that do not fit the strategy and explain why

links.title: Will Larson: writing an engineering strategy

nodes.title: Mentoring and raising the bar
nodes.summary: Code review that teaches, pairing, writing guides and growing other engineers. Staff promotions hinge on this.
checklist: Give code review comments that explain why and separate blocking from nits
Pair with a junior on a hard task without taking the keyboard
Write a team guide that answers a recurring question once
Delegate work that stretches someone and support them through it

nodes.title: The staff engineer path
nodes.summary: Archetypes, scope and how staff work differs from senior. Read when you are already senior.
checklist: Name the staff archetypes and which fits you
Explain how staff scope differs from senior scope
Keep a record of impact for promotion conversations
Choose problems that matter to the business, not just interesting ones

nodes.title: Frontend system design rounds
nodes.summary: The senior bar: clarify scope, propose an architecture, go deep on two hard parts and state trade-offs clearly.
checklist: Run the RADIO steps: requirements, architecture, data model, interface, optimisations
Clarify functional and non-functional requirements in the first five minutes
Draw components, data flow and client-server API in one diagram
Go deep on performance, accessibility and offline or error states
Close with trade-offs, risks and what you would do next

links.title: GreatFrontEnd: front end system design playbook
Front End Interview Handbook: system design

nodes.title: Practice cases: feed, typeahead, grid, chat
nodes.summary: Most frontend system design rounds reuse a handful of prompts. Practise each one end to end out loud until the hard parts feel routine.
checklist: Design an infinite news feed with cursor pagination, virtualisation and optimistic likes
Design typeahead with debouncing, caching, race handling and keyboard accessibility
Design a data grid with 100,000 rows, sorting, filtering and column virtualisation
Design a chat client with realtime delivery, ordering and offline drafts
Time-box each case to 40 minutes and review what you missed
